1. The present first appeals and cross objections arise out of the judgement and award dated 31.08.2018 passed in Land Acquisition Reference Case Nos.1458-1498 of 2011, wherein and whereby reference Court has awarded additional compensation of Rs.2036.64/- per sq.mtr. for the agricultural land, which is not road touch and Rs.2345.22/- per sq.mtr. for the agricultural land,
which is road touch land of village Palodar, Dist.Mehsana, which was acquired by the acquiring body for construction of Mehsana Bypass NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2608/2020 ORDER DATED:

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: For acquiring the land of Palodar village, Section 4 notification under the Land acquisition Act, 1894 (for short "the Act") was issued on 04.08.2008 and Section 6 notification was published on 25.04.2009.

The Special Land Acquisition Officer vide award dated 31.12.2010 awarded Rs.33/- per sq.mtr. for agricultural land, which is not road touch and Rs.38/- per sq.mtr. for agricultural land, which is road touch.
The claimants demanded Rs.5000/- per sq.mtr.
Being aggrieved, the acquiring body has filed the first appeals, whereas the claimants have filed cross objections seeking enhanced compensation.

2. Learned AGP for the acquiring body has submitted that the reference court has fallen in error in enhancing the compensation since the Special Land Acquisition Officer has appropriately awarded the amount of Rs.33/- per sq.mtr. for agricultural non-road touch land and Rs.38/- per sq.mtr. for agricultural road touch land vide award dated 31.12.2010.

He has further submitted that considering the quality and fertility of the acquired lands, prospect of the development of the village etc., the Special Land Acquisition Officer has precisely determined the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2608/2020 ORDER DATED: 18/04/2023 undefined award and hence, the reference Court could not have interfered with the same.
Thus, it is submitted that the impugned judgement and award may be quashed and set aside.

3. In response to the aforesaid submissions, learned advocate Mr.Prajapati has submitted that the reference Court, while placing reliance on the judgement and award passed with regard to adjoining village Panchot, incorrectly determined or deducted 10% amount for the road touch land and as per the settled proposition of law, instead of 10% deduction, 5% was required to be deducted for the road touch land and hence, the compensation, which is awarded for the road touch land is required to be enhanced.

He has submitted that this Court vide judgement dated 05.04.2023 passed in First Appeal No.4460 of 2018 and allied matters, rejected the first appeals filed by the acquiring body with regard to compensation of the lands of village Panchot and has confirmed the judgement and award passed by the reference Court awarding additional compensation of Rs.2707/- per sq.mtr. for the road touch land and Rs.2088/- per sq.mtr. for the non-road touch land and hence, the present first appeals are accordingly required to be rejected and cross objections

sentences.text: Heard the learned advocates for the respective parties and also perused the documents as pointed out by them.

5. The acquiring body for the purpose of construction of Mehsana Bypass Road has acquired the land of village Palodar, for which Section 4 notification was issued on 04.08.2008 and Section 6 notification was issued on 25.04.2009.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer awarded Rs.33/- per sq.mtr. for the agricultural non-road touch land and Rs.38/- per sq.mtr. for the agricultural road touch land vide its award dated 31.12.2010.
The claimants, being aggrieved, initiated the reference proceedings.

The reference Court, while placing reliance on the judgement and award below Exh.54 of adjoining village Panchot, for which Section 4 notification was issued on 11.02.2009 has determined the amount of award and compensation.

6. The reference Court in case of land acquired for adjoining village Panchot awarded the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2608/2020 ORDER DATED: 18/04/2023 undefined additional compensation of Rs.2707/- per sq.mtr. for road touch land and Rs.2088/- per sq.mtr. for other parcel of land and the same was subject matter of challenge before this Court by the acquiring body in First Appeal Nos.4406 of 2018 and allied matters.

This Court has dismissed the first appeals vide judgement and order dated 05.04.2023 by observing thus:
"7.
We have perused Exh.164, District Valuation Committee Report, which is of 8.10.2004.
It reveals that for the Village-Nagalpur, District Valuation Committee has determined the price of the land at Rs.3,000/- per sq.mtr.

A perusal of Exh.149,
which pertains to Sale Deed dated 30.10.2007 of Village- Nagalpur for Rs.2,06,40,000/- for 6880 sq.mtrs. of land, the Reference Court has determined the amount of compensation at Rs.3,000/- per sq.mtr. by taking the average.
A perusal of map at Exh.157, indicates that Village-Nagalpur is adjoining to Village- Panchot.
The by-pass highway for which the land is acquired passes through Village-Panchot.
The distance between Nagalpur and Village Panchot is approximately 8 to 9 kilometers.
However, it is noticed by us that Village-Nagalpur falls within the outskirts of Mehsana city.

Thus, looking to the distance between Village-Nagalpur and Village-Panchot and topography of the area, we are of the considered opinion that since by-pass highway for which lands were acquired passes through Village-Panchot, whereas Village- Nagalpur is situated at the outskirts of Mehsana city, deduction of 20% by the Reference Court from the final amount of Rs.3,000/-
was appropriate.

On the evaluation of the aforesaid evidence, we are of the considered opinion that the Reference Court has not committed any error in determining amount of Rs.3,000/- per sq.mtr. towards land acquired at Village-Panchot.
The 20% deduction from Rs.3,000/- would come to Rs.2,400/- per sq.mtr.

Thereafter, further deduction of 40% is made from the aforesaid NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2608/2020 ORDER DATED: 18/04/2023 undefined amount of Rs.2,400/- which pertains to 30% for N.A.Purpose and 10% deduction of smallness of plot, which would come to Rs.960/-.

Hence, amount of Rs.1440 (Rs.2400 - Land Acquisition Officer vs Patel Ghanshyambhai Narandas on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84824410/
4 Rs.960) is arrived at.

sentences.text:
The District Valuation Committee Report is of 8.10.2004 and,
in the present case, Section 4 Notification was issued on 11.2.2009 and as the Reference Court has considered difference of four years, four months and four days,
and has considered 10% rise of market value per annum and had determined the amount of Rs.2,178.57 per sq.mtr. (Rs.1440 + 144 = Rs.1584/-) and after lapse of four years period, it would come to Rs.2178.57.

The Special Land Acquisition Officer has awarded Rs.91/- per sq.mtr. and hence, the amount of compensation would come to Rs.2087.57 (2178.57 - Rs.91), which if rounded off will be Rs.2088/- per sq.mtr. for the other land, which is not road touch.
For the road touch land, the Reference Court has calculated and awarded Rs.2707/- per sq.mtr.

i.e. Rs.2844.95 awarded by the reference Court deducting Rs.118/- awarded by Special Land Acquisition Officer,
which is rounded off to Rs.2707/- per sq.mtr.
8.

It is also noticed by this Court that the Reference Court has determined the amount of Rs.2707/- per sq.mtr. for road touch land on the basis of the award passed by Special Land Acquisition Officer of Rs.118/- per sq.mtr.

Thus, in the considered opinion of this Court, after considering the oral as well as documentary evidence, the Reference Court has precisely concluded and awarded the amount, which do not require any interference, as we do not find any illegality or infirmity in the judgment and award.
We are not convinced to alter the compensation, hence, these First Appeals as well as Cross Objections do not require any interference and the same are dismissed.
Record and Proceedings be sent back to the concerned trial Court forthwith."

7. Section 4 notification for village Panchot was issued on 11.02.2009, whereas in the present case,
for acquiring land of village Palodar, Section 4 notification was issued on 04.08.2008.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2608/2020 ORDER DATED: 18/04/2023 undefined
The topography of Mehsana Taluka reveals that village Panchot and village Palodar share common boundary and are adjoining to each-other.

The market value of village Panchot is determined at Rs.2178.57/- per sq.mtr. for agricultural non- road touch land and Rs.2844.95/- per sq.mtr. for road touch land and since there is time gap of 6 months between two notifications i.e. Section 4 notification dated 04.08.2008 for village Palodar and Section 4 notification dated 11.02.2009 for village Panchot,

instead of deducting 5% for the road touch agricultural land, the reference Court has deducted 10%
amount.
It is not in dispute that as per the settled proposition of law, 5% was required to be deducted from the amount of compensation looking to the difference of land.

Thus, the reference Court has fallen in error by deducting 10% for the road touch land instead of 5%, whereas the reference Court has appropriately and precisely deducted 5% from the agricultural non-road touch land hence, looking to the difference of 6 months, 5% is required to be deducted from the amount of Rs.2707/- per sq.mtr. from the land acquired of village Palodar, which comes to Rs.2571.65/- per sq.mtr.

The reference Court has awarded Rs.2383/- per sq.mtr. for road touch land and accordingly,
the amount of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2608/2020 ORDER DATED: 18/04/2023 undefined compensation is to be enhanced by Rs.188/- per sq.mtr. for the road touch land.

sentences.text: With regard to non-road touch land, this Court does not find any illegality or infirmity in determining the value of such land by the reference Court.
9. Accordingly, 50% amount of the awarded amount, which is already deposited before the reference Court shall be disbursed to the claimants, after due verification.

The differential amount, as mentioned hereinabove for the road touch lands, shall be deposited before the trial Court with statutory interest as awarded by the Reference Court within a period of three months and on such deposit, the claimants shall be disbursed such amount.
10. The first appeals are dismissed.
Cross objections are allowed to the aforesaid extend.
